title: HTTP caching
subtitle: How a browser or CDN decides to reuse a response — RFC 9111
source: RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching), from model knowledge — not checked against the RFC text line by line
summary: A cache stores responses and reuses them while they are **fresh**. When a response is **stale**, the cache asks the origin server if it is still valid. This is **revalidation**.

summary.title: The one idea to keep
summary.text: Freshness decides *whether to ask*. Validators (`ETag`, `Last-Modified`) decide *what to ask*.

legend.label: Inferred
legend.description: Common practice, not required by the RFC

sections.title: What gets stored
sections.summary: A cache can store a response only when the response allows it.
blocks: `Cache-Control: no-store` forbids storing. `private` forbids **shared** caches (CDNs, proxies) but allows the browser cache.

sections.title: Freshness
sections.summary: A stored response is fresh while its age is below its freshness lifetime.
blocks: The lifetime comes from `max-age` (or `s-maxage` for shared caches), then from `Expires`.

blocks.text: If none is present, a cache may guess a **heuristic** lifetime. The RFC suggests 10% of the time since `Last-Modified`, but does not require it.

sections.title: Revalidation
sections.summary: A stale response is checked, not thrown away.
blocks: The cache sends a conditional request: `If-None-Match` with the `ETag`, or `If-Modified-Since` with `Last-Modified`.
A `304 Not Modified` answer means the stored copy is still good; the cache refreshes its metadata and serves it. See [[states:entry.revalidating|the entry states]].

sections.title: no-cache is not no-store

blocks.text: no-cache: the response MUST NOT be used to satisfy any other request without forwarding it for validation

blocks: So `no-cache` means *store it, but always ask first*. People often confuse it with `no-store`.

scenarios.title: If the response says no-store
scenarios.summary: Amber = behaves differently. Red dashed = never happens. Grey = unchanged.

store_new.note: Nothing is stored, so the next request is a miss again.

fresh.note: There is never a stored copy to judge.

serve.label:
Serve
(pass-through)
serve.note: The body goes straight to the client.

machines.title: A cache entry over time
machines.summary: One stored response moves between these states.

states.label: Stale
detail: Must be revalidated before use, unless `stale-while-revalidate` or `stale-if-error` allows otherwise.

states.label: Revalidating
detail: A conditional request is in flight.

states.label: Evicted
detail: Removed to free space. {{inferred}} Eviction policy (LRU and so on) is up to the implementation.

walkthroughs.title: Follow one request: /logo.png
walkthroughs.intro: The CDN stored `/logo.png` an hour ago with `Cache-Control: max-age=600` and an `ETag`.

steps.title: A request arrives
blocks: The CDN finds the stored response. It was stored 3600 seconds ago.

steps.title: Not yet
blocks: Age 3600 is above `max-age=600`. The copy is **stale**. Serving it without asking breaks the rules (unless `stale-while-revalidate` allows it).

steps.title: It is stale, so revalidate
blocks: The CDN sends `If-None-Match: "abc123"` to the origin.

steps.title: 304 Not Modified
blocks: No body crosses the network. The CDN resets the entry's age and serves the stored logo. Fresh again for 600 seconds.

steps.title: 200 with the new logo
blocks: The CDN replaces the old entry and serves the new body.

questions.title: How long is a response fresh with no lifetime headers?
blocks: The RFC allows a heuristic but only suggests 10% of the time since `Last-Modified`. Browsers and CDNs differ.

questions.title: Do `Vary: *` responses ever hit?
blocks: No. `Vary: *` always fails to match, so every request goes to the origin.

quiz.q: A response has `Cache-Control: no-cache`. Can the browser store it?
choices: Yes, but it must revalidate before every use
explain: `no-cache` means *store, but always ask first*. `no-store` is the one that forbids storing.

quiz.q: The origin answers a conditional request with `304`. What does the cache do?
quiz.answer: Serves its stored copy and refreshes its age — no new body is sent.

suggested_lenses.why: HTTP caching changed across RFC 2616 → 7234 → 9111; a timeline would show what moved.
